listening.title: Campus Card Replacement Desk
listening.focus: Understanding details, fees and collection times
listening.script:
Receptionist: Good morning, Campus Card Services. How can I help you?
Maya: Good morning. I'm Maya Patel, a first-year nursing student. I think I lost my campus card yesterday.
Receptionist: I'm sorry to hear that. I can help you get a replacement. When did you last have it?
Maya: I used it to enter the library at about 3 p.m. yesterday. I put it in my jacket pocket, but it's not there now.
Receptionist: Have you checked the library lost property desk?
Maya: Yes, I went there this morning, but they don't have it.
Receptionist: Okay, we will block your old card so no one else can use it. Can I have your student number?
Maya: Yes, it's N84729.
Receptionist: Thank you, I've blocked card N84729. Do you use the card for building access?
Maya: Yes, I need it for my dormitory and the cafeteria every day.
Receptionist: I understand. There is a fee for a new card. It's $25 for a replacement — sorry, $15 for the first time you lose it.
Maya: That's good. $15 is okay. How do I pay?
Receptionist: You can pay at the cashier next door by cash or card. Then bring the receipt back here.
Maya: And when will the new card be ready?
Receptionist: If you pay today before 2 p.m., you can collect it tomorrow morning after 10 a.m. from this desk.
Maya: Tomorrow after 10, great. What time do you close?
Receptionist: We are open until 5 p.m. Monday to Thursday — actually 4 p.m. on Friday, so please come early tomorrow.
Maya: Okay, I'll come at 10:30. What should I bring?
Receptionist: Please bring your passport or driving licence and the payment receipt. We will take a new photo here if needed.
Maya: Perfect. So I pay today, come tomorrow after 10 with my passport and receipt.
Receptionist: Exactly. And please check your email — we will send a confirmation when it's ready.
Maya: Thank you very much for your help.
Receptionist: You're welcome, Maya. See you tomorrow.

reading.title: Student First-Aid Course Timetable
reading.focus: Understanding main ideas, schedule and requirements
reading.passage:
The University Health Centre offers a free First-Aid Course for all students this term. The aim is to give students basic skills to help in emergencies on campus and at home. The Health Centre has run this course for five years and many students have completed it. The course leaders say that learning first aid increases confidence in emergencies. For example, they describe how a student used chest compressions to help a visitor who fell in the library last year.

The course runs for three Saturdays in November: 8, 15 and 22 November. Each session is from 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. in Room B12 of the Health Building. There is a 15-minute break at 11 a.m. with tea and biscuits provided. Students must attend all three sessions to receive a certificate. If you miss a session, you will need to join the next term's course.

Session 1 on 8 November covers calling for help and checking breathing. Students will practise how to put someone in the recovery position and how to stay calm until help arrives. There will be time for questions at the end.

Session 2 on 15 November focuses on cuts, burns and choking. The teacher will show how to clean a small cut and how to cool a burn with water for ten minutes. Students will also practise what to do if someone is choking, including back blows.

Session 3 on 22 November is about CPR and using a defibrillator. A defibrillator is a machine that can help restart the heart. Students will work in pairs to practise CPR on models. No real medical experience is needed, and all steps are explained slowly.

The course is taught by two nurses from the Health Centre, Anna Grey and Tom Hall. All materials are provided, but students should wear comfortable clothes and bring water. At the end of Session 3, students who attended every session will take a short quiz and get a First-Aid Certificate valid for three years.

To join, students must register online by 1 November. Places are limited to 20 students per term, and the course is very popular, so early booking is advised. Last term all places were filled two weeks before the deadline. Students can find the registration link on the university website. The Health Centre staff are happy to answer questions by phone during office hours. For more information, email healthcentre@university.ac.uk or visit the Health Centre desk on the ground floor.

exercises.title: Student First-Aid Course Timetable
exercises.focus: Understanding main ideas, schedule and requirements
exercises.passage:
The University Health Centre offers a free First-Aid Course for all students this term. The aim is to give students basic skills to help in emergencies on campus and at home. The Health Centre has run this course for five years and many students have completed it. The course leaders say that learning first aid increases confidence in emergencies. For example, they describe how a student used chest compressions to help a visitor who fell in the library last year.

The course runs for three Saturdays in November: 8, 15 and 22 November. Each session is from 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. in Room B12 of the Health Building. There is a 15-minute break at 11 a.m. with tea and biscuits provided. Students must attend all three sessions to receive a certificate. If you miss a session, you will need to join the next term's course.

Session 1 on 8 November covers calling for help and checking breathing. Students will practise how to put someone in the recovery position and how to stay calm until help arrives. There will be time for questions at the end.

Session 2 on 15 November focuses on cuts, burns and choking. The teacher will show how to clean a small cut and how to cool a burn with water for ten minutes. Students will also practise what to do if someone is choking, including back blows.

Session 3 on 22 November is about CPR and using a defibrillator. A defibrillator is a machine that can help restart the heart. Students will work in pairs to practise CPR on models. No real medical experience is needed, and all steps are explained slowly.

The course is taught by two nurses from the Health Centre, Anna Grey and Tom Hall. All materials are provided, but students should wear comfortable clothes and bring water. At the end of Session 3, students who attended every session will take a short quiz and get a First-Aid Certificate valid for three years.

To join, students must register online by 1 November. Places are limited to 20 students per term, and the course is very popular, so early booking is advised. Last term all places were filled two weeks before the deadline. Students can find the registration link on the university website. The Health Centre staff are happy to answer questions by phone during office hours. For more information, email healthcentre@university.ac.uk or visit the Health Centre desk on the ground floor.
exercises.prompt: Which is given as an example of first-aid help?
exercises.explanation: The library incident with chest compressions is presented as an example. Increased confidence is the leaders' claim, not the example.

writingPrompts.focus: clear overview, direct comparisons, familiar academic context
writingPrompts.prompt:
The table below shows the number of students who attended a voluntary campus first-aid workshop at Parkside College in March, April and May 2024, and the main skill each student chose to practise. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

Data:
March 2024 – Total 42 students: Basic bandaging 14, CPR practice 18, Recovery position 10
April 2024 – Total 58 students: Basic bandaging 20, CPR practice 22, Recovery position 16
May 2024 – Total 65 students: Basic bandaging 18, CPR practice 30, Recovery position 17

writingPrompts.task: Task 1 · Reasons for Replacing Student Access Cards
writingPrompts.focus: clear main trends, direct evidence, simple explanations
writingPrompts.prompt:
The chart below shows the number of student access cards replaced at Greenfield College for four different reasons in 2023 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

Data for 2023 / 2024:
Lost card: 120 / 95
Damaged card: 45 / 60
Stolen card: 20 / 15
Name or course change: 10 / 25
Total replacements: 195 in 2023, 195 in 2024

writingPrompts.task: Task 2 · Learning from a Neighbourhood Market Visit
writingPrompts.focus: clear position, direct evidence, familiar academic context
writingPrompts.prompt: Some teachers organise a visit to a local neighbourhood market to help students learn about food, prices and local culture. Others think students can learn the same things in the classroom and a visit is not necessary. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons and examples from your own experience. You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words.

writingPrompts.task: Task 2 · Compulsory First-Aid Training on Campus
writingPrompts.focus: clear main ideas, accurate simple explanations, direct support
writingPrompts.prompt: Some people think every university student should attend a basic first-aid workshop during their first year. Others think this training should be optional and only for students who are interested. Do you agree or disagree that first-aid training should be compulsory for all students? Give reasons for your answer and include examples from your own experience or knowledge. You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words.

writingPrompts.task: Task 2 · Fees for Replacing a Student Access Card
writingPrompts.focus: advantages and disadvantages, clear opinion, simple explanations
writingPrompts.prompt: At many colleges, students have to pay a small fee, for example $10 or $15, to replace a lost or damaged access card. Some students think this fee is fair because it teaches responsibility. Others think the college should replace cards for free. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of charging a fee for replacement cards and give your own opinion. You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words.

speakingPrompts.focus: familiar everyday topics, short personal answers
speakingPrompts.prompt:
Answer the following questions with short, clear answers. Give a reason or example for each answer.
1. Do you like visiting local markets? Why or why not?
2. How often do you go to a market or small shop in your neighbourhood?
3. What do you usually buy at a market?
4. Do you prefer markets or supermarkets? Why?

speakingPrompts.task: Part 1 · Campus Life and Student Cards
speakingPrompts.prompt:
Answer the following questions with short, clear answers. Give a reason or example for each answer.
1. Do you use a student card or ID card every day?
2. What do you use your student card for?
3. Have you ever lost an important card? What happened?
4. Is it easy to get help on your campus if you have a problem with your card?

speakingPrompts.task: Part 2 · Cue card · Describe a Visit to a Neighbourhood Market
speakingPrompts.focus: clear description, direct evidence, simple explanation of why it was useful
speakingPrompts.prompt:
Describe a visit you made to a neighbourhood market or local market. You will have one minute to prepare and should speak for one to two minutes.

You should say:
• when and where you went
• who you went with
• what you saw and did there
• and explain why this visit was interesting or useful for you.

You can make notes in your preparation time.

speakingPrompts.task: Part 3 · Learning Practical Skills Outside the Classroom
speakingPrompts.focus: reasons and evaluation, comparing classroom and real-world learning
speakingPrompts.prompt:
Discuss the following questions more fully. Give reasons, compare ideas, and explain your opinions.
1. Why do some teachers take students to places like markets or workshops outside the classroom?
2. What are the advantages of learning practical skills such as first aid at college?
3. Should practical workshops be compulsory for all students? Why or why not?
4. How can colleges make outside visits more useful for students who are not very interested?

speakingPrompts.task: Part 3 · Campus Rules and Student Responsibility
speakingPrompts.focus: evaluation of fairness, reasons for rules and fees
speakingPrompts.prompt:
Discuss the following questions more fully. Give reasons and evaluate different opinions.
1. Why do colleges charge a fee when students need to replace a lost access card?
2. Do you think a small fee helps students be more responsible? Why or why not?
3. What is a fair way for a college to deal with students who lose their cards many times?
4. How can colleges help new students understand and follow campus rules better?
